title: MRI Pre-Authorization Procedure for Insured Patients
content: All insured patients requiring MRI investigations must obtain pre-authorization from their TPA (Third Party Administrator) before the scan is performed, except in life-threatening emergencies. The front office or TPA desk must verify the patient's active insurance policy via the HIS Insurance Module and confirm MRI diagnostics are covered under the plan. A pre-authorization request must be submitted through the insurer's TPA portal with the referring physician's name, diagnosis code (ICD-10), procedure code, and scheduled date. Authorization turnaround is typically 2–4 hours for routine cases and must be received in writing (email or portal acknowledgment) before scheduling the scan. If authorization is rejected, the TPA escalation team must be notified immediately and the patient must be counselled on out-of-pocket options.

title: Discharge Summary Documentation Standards
content: A discharge summary must be completed by the treating physician within 24 hours of patient discharge and uploaded to the HIS under the patient's encounter record. The summary must include: primary and secondary diagnoses (ICD-10 coded), procedures performed, medications prescribed at discharge, follow-up instructions, and the patient's condition at discharge. The discharge coordinator must verify the summary is complete and signed before issuing the final discharge bill. All discharge documents must be provided to the patient in both physical and digital formats via the patient portal. Incomplete discharge summaries must be flagged to the Medical Superintendent's office within 48 hours.

title: Billing Correction Policy for Amounts Over $500
content: Billing corrections involving amounts greater than $500 require supervisor approval before any adjustment is applied to the patient account. The billing staff must raise a correction request in the HIS Billing Module with a detailed justification, the original charge code, corrected amount, and supporting documentation (e.g., service order, physician note). The Billing Supervisor must review and approve or reject within 4 business hours. Approved corrections must be countersigned by the Finance Controller if the amount exceeds $2,000. All corrections are logged in the immutable audit trail and are subject to quarterly review by the Internal Audit team. Corrections below $500 may be processed directly by senior billing staff without escalation.

title: ICU Visitor Policy
content: ICU visitation is restricted to two immediate family members per patient per visit to prevent infection and minimize patient disturbance. Visiting hours are 10:00–11:00 AM and 5:00–6:00 PM only; exceptions require written approval from the ICU Attending Physician. All visitors must sign the visitor register at the ICU nursing station, wear provided PPE (gown and gloves), and sanitize hands before entry. Children under 12 years of age are not permitted in the ICU under any circumstances. Visitors showing symptoms of respiratory illness, fever, or active infection must be denied entry and directed to the hospital's General OPD.

title: Medical Records Release to Patient or Authorized Representative
content: Patients or their authorized legal representatives may request their medical records by submitting Form MR-REQ-01 at the Medical Records Department with valid government-issued photo ID. Records are typically provided within 5 working days of a verified request; urgent requests (e.g., second opinions, legal matters) are processed within 24 hours with HOD approval. Records must not be released to third parties without a signed patient authorization form or valid court order. Digital copies may be provided via the patient portal after identity verification. All record releases must be logged with the requestor's identity, date, purpose, and staff member who processed the request.

title: IT Access Provisioning for New Hospital Staff
content: New staff IT access must be requested by the department HOD using Form IT-ACC-01 submitted to the IT Help Desk at least 48 hours before the staff member's start date. Access levels are mapped to the employee's role as defined in the Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) matrix maintained by IT Administration. The IT team will provision HIS login credentials, email account, and role-specific module access within 24 hours of receiving a complete request. Temporary passwords must be changed upon first login; failure to do so within 48 hours triggers an automatic account lock. All access provisioning events are logged in the IT Audit System and reviewed monthly.

title: Pharmacy Stock-Out Emergency Protocol
content: When a critical drug is out of stock, the Pharmacy In-Charge must immediately notify the treating physician and nursing station, and simultaneously contact at least two approved alternative suppliers from the vendor list. An emergency procurement request must be raised in the HIS Pharmacy Module within 30 minutes of confirming stock-out. If the drug cannot be sourced within 4 hours, the case must be escalated to the Medical Superintendent for clinical decision-making regarding therapeutic substitution. All stock-out incidents must be documented in the Pharmacy Incident Register with time of discovery, drug name, quantity required, and resolution steps taken. A root-cause analysis must be submitted to Pharmacy Management within 48 hours.

title: Patient Bed Allocation Procedure
content: Bed allocation is managed through the HIS Bed Management Module and must reflect real-time occupancy at all times. Admission requests are triaged by the Admissions Desk based on clinical priority: Emergency admissions take precedence, followed by planned surgical cases, and then elective admissions. Bed type allocation (General, Semi-Private, Private, ICU) must align with the physician's bed request form and patient's insurance coverage or payment category. Ward staff must update bed status in HIS within 15 minutes of patient transfer, discharge, or admission. Any bed disputes between departments must be escalated to the Bed Manager or on-call Operations Manager.

title: CT Scan Scheduling and Intravenous Contrast Protocol
content: CT scans requiring intravenous (IV) contrast must be preceded by a serum creatinine test to assess renal function; patients with creatinine above 1.5 mg/dL require Radiology Physician sign-off before contrast administration. Scheduling must be done through the HIS Radiology Module by the requesting department, with at least 2 hours' notice for routine scans and immediate priority for emergency cases. Patients must be nil-by-mouth (NPO) for 4 hours prior to contrast CT; nursing staff must verify and document NPO compliance before sending the patient to Radiology. The Radiology Technologist must confirm allergy history (especially iodine/shellfish) and obtain written consent for contrast use. Any adverse contrast reactions must be reported immediately to the Radiology Attending and documented in the patient's HIS record.

title: Specimen Collection Guidelines for Laboratory Tests
content: All laboratory specimens must be collected using the correct labelled vacutainer or container as specified in the Lab Test Reference Guide available on the HIS Laboratory Module. Specimen labels must include: patient MRN, full name, date and time of collection, and the ordering physician's ID. Blood specimens must be collected by a trained phlebotomist or registered nurse; collections by unauthorized personnel are not permitted. Specimens must be transported to the laboratory within the time limits specified per test type (e.g., blood gas analysis within 15 minutes, routine blood within 2 hours). Mislabeled, hemolyzed, or improperly stored specimens will be rejected; the requesting department must be notified within 30 minutes of rejection.

title: Biomedical Equipment Downtime Reporting Procedure
content: Any failure or malfunction of critical biomedical equipment (ventilators, infusion pumps, ECG machines, imaging systems) must be reported to the Biomedical Engineering Department immediately via the HIS Asset Management Module or the Biomedical Help Desk (ext. 4400). The reporting staff must provide: equipment ID, location (ward/room), nature of fault, time of failure, and whether a patient was affected. Biomedical Engineering must acknowledge the report within 15 minutes and dispatch a technician within 30 minutes for life-critical equipment. A substitute device must be arranged by the ward/department head while repairs are underway. All equipment downtime events must be logged and included in the monthly Equipment Reliability Report.

title: Insurance Claim Submission Procedure to TPA
content: Insurance claims for inpatient admissions must be submitted to the TPA within 24 hours of patient discharge using the claim form specific to the insurer. Required documents include: discharge summary, itemized bill, investigation reports, pre-authorization approval letter, and copies of all consent forms. Claims must be uploaded to the insurer's portal and a physical set sent by courier within the same business day. The TPA Desk must track claim status daily and escalate any claims pending beyond 5 business days to the TPA Escalation Manager. Partial approvals or rejections must be communicated to the Billing Department within 2 hours of receipt for patient counselling.

title: Patient Transfer Between Hospital Wards
content: Intra-hospital patient transfers require a transfer request entered in the HIS by the attending physician with the reason for transfer, receiving ward, and patient's current clinical status. The receiving ward must confirm bed availability before the transfer is initiated; transfers cannot proceed without receiving ward confirmation. The transferring nurse must complete a clinical handover using the SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) format and document it in the patient's HIS record. All essential medications, patient belongings, and clinical files must accompany the patient. Transfers of ICU patients to general wards require attending physician sign-off and must be completed during daytime hours (7 AM–9 PM) except in emergencies.

title: OPD Appointment Scheduling Policy
content: OPD appointments must be scheduled through the HIS OPD Module or the patient-facing appointment portal; walk-in patients are accommodated only if slots are available after portal bookings are filled. Each OPD slot is 15 minutes; complex consultations or second opinions may be booked as double slots with prior physician consent. Appointment reminders are automatically sent via SMS 24 hours before the scheduled time. Cancellations by the patient must be made at least 2 hours before the appointment to free the slot for another patient; repeated no-shows (3 or more) must be flagged to the Front Office Manager. Urgent referrals from Emergency or ward physicians receive priority scheduling within the same day.

title: Incident Reporting and Near-Miss Documentation
content: All adverse events, incidents, and near-misses must be reported within 2 hours of occurrence using the Incident Report Form in the HIS Quality Module or the physical form available at each nursing station. The report must include: date, time, location, persons involved, nature of the incident, immediate actions taken, and the reporter's identity. Sentinel events (unexpected patient death, serious injury) must trigger an immediate verbal report to the Quality & Patient Safety officer and Medical Superintendent. Near-miss events (no harm occurred but could have) are equally important and must be reported without fear of punitive action to encourage a safety culture. Root cause analysis must be completed within 72 hours for major incidents and presented to the Quality Committee monthly.

title: Financial Assistance and Patient Waiver Application
content: Patients experiencing financial hardship may apply for a billing waiver by submitting Form FIN-WAV-01 with supporting income documentation to the Billing Department. Waivers of up to 25% may be approved by the Billing Supervisor; amounts between 25–50% require Finance Controller approval; waivers above 50% require the CEO's authorization. All waiver applications must be processed within 24 hours of receiving complete documentation. Approved waivers are applied directly to the patient's account and noted in the HIS Billing Module with the approver's employee ID. Waiver decisions must be communicated to the patient in writing and are final; re-applications require new documentation.

title: Radiology Report Turnaround Time Standards
content: Radiology reports must be finalized and uploaded to the HIS within defined turnaround times: Emergency/stat studies within 1 hour, urgent studies within 4 hours, and routine outpatient studies within 24 hours of scan completion. Preliminary reports may be provided verbally or via HIS messaging for emergency cases, but the formal signed report must follow within the stated timeframe. Any delay beyond these standards must be flagged to the Head of Radiology with documented justification. Referring physicians must be notified immediately of any critical or unexpected findings regardless of the study's priority level. Radiology reports must be reviewed and countersigned by a board-certified Radiologist before being marked final in the system.

title: HIS Downtime Contingency Procedure
content: In the event of planned or unplanned HIS downtime, the IT Helpdesk must immediately notify all department heads via the hospital broadcast system and group message. All departments must switch to pre-printed downtime forms available in the Downtime Folder (physical, at each nursing station and front desk) within 5 minutes of notification. Patient registrations, medication orders, lab results, and billing transactions during downtime must be recorded on paper and entered into HIS within 2 hours of system restoration. Lab and Radiology must maintain physical logs of all tests ordered and results issued during downtime. IT must provide hourly status updates during unplanned outages; planned maintenance windows must be communicated at least 48 hours in advance.

title: Patient Consent Form Requirements
content: Informed consent must be obtained for all surgical procedures, invasive diagnostic tests, administration of blood products, and participation in clinical research, using the department-specific consent forms in the HIS Forms Library. Consent must be obtained by the treating physician in the patient's preferred language; an interpreter must be arranged if needed. The signed consent form must be scanned and uploaded to the patient's HIS record before the procedure begins. Emergency procedures may proceed without prior written consent if the patient is incapacitated and no legal representative is reachable, but verbal consent from the available family must be documented by two witnesses. Consent may be withdrawn by the patient at any time; withdrawal must be documented and the treating physician notified immediately.

title: Biomedical Equipment Preventive Maintenance Schedule
content: All biomedical equipment must undergo preventive maintenance (PM) as per the manufacturer's recommended schedule and the hospital's annual PM calendar maintained in the HIS Asset Management Module. Critical life-support equipment (ventilators, defibrillators, infusion pumps) must be serviced every 3 months; diagnostic imaging equipment (X-ray, ultrasound, CT, MRI) every 6 months; general ward equipment annually. PM work orders are auto-generated by HIS 30 days before the due date; the Biomedical team must complete and close each work order within 7 days of the due date. Equipment out of PM compliance must be taken offline until serviced; the ward head must be notified immediately. PM completion certificates must be filed in the Equipment File and are subject to NABH accreditation audits.

title: Controlled Substance Dispensing and Double-Check Protocol
content: All Schedule H1 and narcotic medications must be dispensed only on a valid physician's prescription bearing the prescriber's registration number, patient MRN, and diagnosis. Two pharmacists must independently verify the prescription, drug, dose, and quantity before dispensing — this double-check must be documented with both pharmacists' initials in the Controlled Substance Register. Controlled substances must be stored in a locked, double-key cabinet with access restricted to licensed pharmacists; the cabinet must be reconciled at every shift handover. Any discrepancy between dispensed quantity and register entry must be reported immediately to the Chief Pharmacist and Security within 15 minutes. Monthly audits of the Controlled Substance Register are mandatory and must be submitted to the Pharmacy Committee and the hospital's Drug & Therapeutics Committee.

title: Medication Reconciliation on Patient Admission
content: A complete medication reconciliation must be performed for every patient within 4 hours of admission using the HIS Pharmacy Module. The admitting nurse or pharmacist must compile a Best Possible Medication History (BPMH) by interviewing the patient and/or caregiver and cross-referencing with previous HIS records, referral documents, and any medications the patient brought to hospital. The BPMH must be reviewed by the treating physician, who will reconcile current home medications with new inpatient orders, documenting any changes, continuations, or substitutions with clinical rationale. High-alert medications (anticoagulants, insulin, concentrated electrolytes) require a second pharmacist verification before any order is processed. Reconciliation must be repeated at each care transition: transfer between wards, change in attending physician, and at discharge.

title: Critical Value Reporting Protocol
content: Laboratory critical values (also called panic values) are results so abnormal they may indicate a life-threatening condition requiring immediate clinical action. The Laboratory must call the critical value directly to the treating physician or responsible nurse within 15 minutes of result verification; the HIS alert must be triggered simultaneously. The caller must document: result, time called, person notified, their acknowledgment, and the read-back confirmation in the LIS. If the responsible clinician cannot be reached within 15 minutes, the call must escalate to the ward charge nurse and then to the Medical Superintendent. Critical value thresholds (e.g., serum potassium <2.5 or >6.5 mmol/L, blood glucose <2.2 or >25 mmol/L, hemoglobin <5 g/dL) are defined in the Lab Critical Value Table maintained by the Laboratory Committee and reviewed annually.

title: Blood Transfusion Request and Pre-Transfusion Testing
content: Blood and blood product transfusion requests must be submitted via the HIS Laboratory Module with the patient's MRN, blood group, cross-match sample, clinical indication, and urgency level. Pre-transfusion testing (group and screen, crossmatch) is mandatory before any non-emergency transfusion; for life-threatening emergencies, O-negative uncrossmatched blood may be issued on verbal physician authorization with written documentation to follow within 15 minutes. The blood bank will prepare and issue units within 45 minutes for urgent requests and 2 hours for routine requests. Transfusion must be administered within 30 minutes of unit issue; units returned to the blood bank after this window will be discarded. Any suspected transfusion reaction (fever, chills, hypotension, rash) must trigger immediate transfusion stoppage, notification to the on-call physician, and a transfusion reaction report filed in HIS within 1 hour.

title: Discharge Planning and Multidisciplinary Case Review
content: Discharge planning must commence at admission for all inpatients expected to stay more than 48 hours, led by the Case Manager assigned to the patient. The Case Manager coordinates a multidisciplinary care conference within 24 hours of admission for complex cases involving multiple specialties, social issues, or anticipated long-stay. Anticipated discharge date must be entered in HIS at admission and updated daily. Social work referral must be initiated within 24 hours for patients with identified social risk factors (homelessness, domestic abuse, caregiver absence, financial hardship). The discharge plan must address: post-discharge care setting, follow-up appointments, equipment needs, medication supply for 30 days, and community health services if required. Patients at high readmission risk (LACE score ≥10) must receive a telephonic follow-up call within 72 hours of discharge.

title: Social Work Referral and Patient Support Services
content: Social work referrals must be initiated by the Case Manager, treating physician, or nursing staff when a patient's social circumstances may affect health outcomes or discharge safety. Referral criteria include: financial inability to pay for treatment, lack of caregiver or support at home, child or elder safeguarding concerns, domestic violence indicators, substance misuse, or chronic homelessness. The Medical Social Worker must assess the referred patient within 4 hours of a CRITICAL referral and within 24 hours for routine referrals, documenting the assessment in the patient's HIS record. Intervention options include: connecting patients to government welfare schemes, arranging NGO support, coordinating with community health workers, and facilitating direct admission to rehabilitation or palliative care facilities. All referral outcomes and interventions must be documented in the Care Coordination Log.

title: Clinical Audit Procedure and Reporting
content: Clinical audits are systematic reviews of clinical practice against defined standards and must be conducted quarterly by each department. The Quality & Accreditation team will publish the annual audit calendar by December 31st for the following year, identifying audit topics, lead departments, and submission deadlines. Each department must conduct at least two clinical audits per year using the standardized audit tool in the HIS Quality Module. Audit results must be presented at the monthly departmental quality meeting and submitted to the Quality Committee within 10 days of completion. Non-conformances identified in audits must have documented corrective action plans with assigned owners and target dates; progress is tracked in the HIS at quarterly intervals. Re-audits are mandatory within 6 months of a major non-conformance to verify that corrective actions have been effective.

title: NABH Accreditation Compliance Standards and Readiness
content: The hospital's NABH accreditation requires continuous compliance with all 10 NABH chapters covering patient care, medication management, infrastructure, HR, quality improvement, and safety. The Quality & Accreditation team is responsible for maintaining a NABH compliance tracker in the HIS Quality Module, updated monthly. Each department head is accountable for the NABH standards applicable to their department and must ensure staff training on relevant standards is completed within 30 days of onboarding and annually thereafter. Internal mock accreditation surveys must be conducted 6 months before each NABH renewal cycle; findings must be fully addressed before the external assessment. All NABH-required policies, procedures, and forms must be reviewed and re-approved annually; version-controlled copies must be available in the HIS Document Management System and at physical display points in each department.

title: Against Medical Advice (AMA) Discharge Procedure
content: When a patient wishes to leave the hospital contrary to the treating physician's recommendation, the nurse or front desk must immediately notify the attending physician and Case Manager. The physician must document the risks of leaving, attempt to address the patient's concerns, and offer alternatives. If the patient persists, they must sign the AMA Discharge Form (Form DIS-AMA-01) witnessed by the physician and a nurse; if the patient refuses to sign, the refusal itself must be documented and witnessed. The final bill must be generated and settled before the patient leaves; unpaid balances at AMA discharge are escalated to the Billing Supervisor. The AMA event must be reported in the HIS Quality Module as a clinical risk event. Patients who leave without any notification (LWBS — Left Without Being Seen) must be documented in the HIS as a security and quality event within 30 minutes of discovery.

title: Death Certification and Mortuary Release Procedure
content: Death of a patient must be certified by the treating physician and documented in the HIS Clinical Module within 1 hour of the event. The Cause of Death Certificate must be completed using the correct ICD-10 cause and immediate/underlying cause fields; all deaths within 24 hours of admission or under anesthesia require Medical Superintendent review. The family must be notified of the death by the attending physician personally; a nursing staff member must provide emotional support and bereavement information. The body may be released to the family after: death certification, clearance of the final bill, and submission of the Mortuary Release Form (Form DIS-MORT-01) signed by a next-of-kin with valid ID. Cases of unnatural death, accidents, or medicolegal cases must be reported to the police before release; legal clearance is mandatory. Autopsy requests (hospital-initiated or family-requested) must be documented and handled per the Post-Mortem Policy.

title: Emergency Patient Arrival and Triage Handoff to Ward
content: Patients arriving at the Emergency Department are triaged using the 5-level Emergency Severity Index (ESI); Level 1 and 2 patients receive immediate care and Level 3–5 are managed per waiting room capacity. When an Emergency patient requires inpatient admission, the Emergency Physician must place the admission order in HIS with bed type, clinical priority, and isolation requirements. The Front Office Admissions Desk must confirm bed availability and allocate within 30 minutes of the admission order for Level 1–2 patients and 60 minutes for Level 3. The Emergency nurse must complete a clinical handover using the SBAR format to the receiving ward nurse before physically transferring the patient; handover must be documented in HIS. All accompanying documents (emergency notes, test results, medications administered) must be transferred with the patient.

title: Outpatient and Inpatient Patient Registration Process
content: All patients must be registered in the HIS at their first contact using a government-issued photo ID and current contact details; patients with previous visits must have their record retrieved and verified rather than re-registered. A unique MRN is generated by the HIS at first registration and is the patient's permanent identifier across all visits and departments. For inpatient admissions, registration must include: admission type (emergency/elective/daycare), admitting physician, expected length of stay, and bed/room preference. Insurance details must be captured at registration; the insurance team must verify coverage electronically within 30 minutes for planned admissions. Patient demographic data must be reviewed and updated at each encounter to ensure accuracy. Consent for treatment and privacy notice acknowledgment must be obtained and scanned into HIS at the time of each admission.

title: Medical Record Amendment and Correction Policy
content: A medical record entry may only be amended by the original author (physician, nurse, or allied health staff) to correct a factual error; all amendments must be transparent, never obliterating the original entry. Amendments in the HIS are versioned automatically; the original entry is retained with a timestamp and the amended version shows the date, time, corrector's ID, and reason for amendment. Paper record corrections must be made by drawing a single line through the error, initialing, dating, and writing the correct entry; correction fluid (Wite-Out) is strictly prohibited. Requests for amendment from patients must be reviewed by the Medical Records Supervisor and the treating physician; unjustified changes must be refused with a written explanation to the patient. Mass or systematic record alterations require Medical Director approval and must be logged as a quality event in the HIS.

title: Cashless Treatment Authorization and Pre-Admission Process
content: Cashless treatment is available for patients with empanelled insurance policies. The patient or family must present the insurance card and a valid photo ID at the TPA Desk on or before admission. The TPA Desk verifies policy validity, sum insured balance, and pre-existing condition exclusions via the insurer's portal before providing a cashless authorization letter. Initial authorization must be obtained before elective procedures; emergency cashless treatment may proceed on verbal insurer authorization if written confirmation is expected within 2 hours. Enhancement requests (for additional treatment costs beyond the initial authorization amount) must be submitted to the TPA as soon as the treating physician identifies the need, with updated clinical notes and revised cost estimate. Cashless authorization does not guarantee full payment; patients must be counselled on any co-payment, non-covered items, or room-rent differences at the time of authorization.

title: Patient Refund Processing Policy
content: Refund requests arise when a patient has overpaid, a planned procedure was not performed, or an insurance payout reduced the patient's liability. All refund requests must be submitted in writing (Form FIN-REF-01) to the Billing Department with the patient's MRN, original receipt number, and reason for refund. Refunds up to $200 may be processed by the Billing Desk within 24 hours after verification of overpayment; amounts between $200–$1,000 require Billing Supervisor approval within 48 hours; amounts exceeding $1,000 require Finance Controller sign-off within 72 hours. Refunds for insured patients require confirmation from the TPA desk that no insurance reclaim is in progress before processing. Refund disbursement must be via the same payment method as the original transaction (card refund for card payments, bank transfer for NEFT/RTGS); cash refunds above $100 require dual-staff authorization. All refunds are recorded in the HIS Billing Module's refund register and reported to Finance monthly.

title: Contrast Reaction Management and Emergency Response
content: All patients receiving iodinated or gadolinium-based contrast agents must be monitored for adverse reactions for a minimum of 30 minutes post-administration. The Radiology Technologist must have immediate access to the contrast reaction emergency kit (containing adrenaline, antihistamines, corticosteroids, IV fluids, and oxygen) at every contrast examination station. Adverse reactions are classified as mild (nausea, urticaria, flushing — managed with observation and antihistamines), moderate (bronchospasm, hypotension — requires physician involvement and IV treatment), and severe/anaphylactic (laryngeal edema, cardiac arrest — requires Code Blue activation). Any moderate or severe reaction must trigger immediate notification of the Radiology Attending and Emergency Medicine team, with Code Blue activated for severe reactions. Post-reaction, a written report must be filed in HIS within 1 hour, the patient's allergy record updated, and the event reported to the Pharmacy and Drug Reaction Committee within 24 hours.

title: Cybersecurity Incident Response Procedure
content: Any suspected or confirmed cybersecurity incident (ransomware, unauthorized access, data breach, phishing attack) must be reported immediately to the IT Security team and the Data Protection Officer by the staff member who discovers it; do not attempt to resolve the incident independently. The IT Security team must assess and classify the incident within 30 minutes: Low (minimal impact, no PHI involved), Medium (operational disruption or potential PHI access), High (confirmed PHI breach, system compromise, or ransomware). High-severity incidents trigger the Cyber Incident Response Plan: isolate affected systems, notify the CIO, activate backup systems, and notify the Data Protection Officer for regulatory assessment within 1 hour. External reporting to the Data Protection Authority must occur within 72 hours of confirming a reportable personal data breach under applicable privacy regulations. All cybersecurity incidents must be documented with timestamps, actions taken, and resolution in the IT Incident Register; a post-incident review must be completed within 2 weeks.

title: Medical Equipment Calibration and Certification Standards
content: All measurement-critical biomedical equipment (infusion pumps, patient monitors, ventilators, pulse oximeters, weighing scales) must be calibrated at the frequency specified in the hospital's Calibration Schedule maintained in the HIS Asset Management Module. Calibration must be performed by a certified biomedical technician or accredited external service provider using traceable reference standards; calibration certificates must be uploaded to HIS within 24 hours of completion. Equipment that fails calibration must be immediately taken out of service, tagged with a clear 'DO NOT USE' sticker, and a substitute arranged; failed calibration events must be reported to the Quality team as a near-miss within 2 hours. All calibration records are subject to inspection during NABH accreditation surveys. Equipment that has not been calibrated within the due period is considered out-of-service for accreditation purposes; the Chief Biomedical Engineer must report any overdue calibrations to the Quality Committee monthly.

title: Fire Safety Protocol and Emergency Evacuation Procedure
content: Upon discovery of fire or smoke, the discovering person must activate the nearest fire alarm pull station and call the hospital emergency line (ext. 0) to report location and nature of the fire. The RACE protocol must be followed: Rescue any patient in immediate danger, Alarm activation, Confine the fire by closing all doors, and Extinguish using appropriate fire extinguisher only if safe to do so. All patient areas must be evacuated following the posted evacuation route to the designated assembly point; non-ambulatory patients are moved horizontally to the nearest fire-rated stairwell enclosure until vertical evacuation by the Fire Department. Staff must NOT use elevators during a fire evacuation. The Facility Manager must conduct a headcount at the assembly point and report to the incident commander within 10 minutes. Fire drills must be conducted at least twice per year per zone; all staff must receive fire safety training annually. Fire extinguishers must be inspected monthly; records must be maintained in the Fire Safety Register.

title: Biomedical Waste Management and Segregation Procedure
content: All clinical waste generated in the hospital must be segregated at the point of generation according to the colour-coded bin system: Yellow bags for infectious/anatomical waste, Red bags for recyclable contaminated plastics, Blue/white boxes for sharps, Black bags for general non-hazardous waste. Sharps (needles, blades, lancets) must be deposited directly into puncture-proof yellow-lidded sharps containers immediately after use; resheathing of needles is strictly prohibited. Infectious waste bags must be filled to no more than 75% capacity, sealed securely, and collected by the housekeeping team every 4 hours or when 75% full, whichever is earlier. Collection, storage, transport, and disposal must comply with applicable biomedical waste regulations; the hospital's licensed common biomedical waste treatment facility contractor must collect waste daily. Staff handling biomedical waste must wear PPE (gloves, apron, mask, eye protection); annual training on waste segregation is mandatory for all clinical and housekeeping staff.

title: HVAC System Maintenance and Air Quality Management
content: The hospital's HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning) systems must maintain indoor air quality standards critical for patient safety, particularly in Operating Theatres (positive pressure, HEPA-filtered, 20+ air changes/hour), ICUs (positive pressure, 12+ air changes/hour), and Isolation Rooms (negative pressure for infectious patients). Filter replacements must follow the manufacturer's schedule: pre-filters monthly, HEPA filters every 6 months or earlier if differential pressure exceeds threshold. Air quality validation tests (particulate counts, microbial sampling) must be performed every 3 months in critical areas (OT, ICU, sterile processing). Any HVAC failure in a critical area must be escalated to the Facility Manager within 15 minutes and a contingency plan activated to maintain sterility; elective procedures must be suspended until air quality is re-validated. Annual comprehensive HVAC maintenance must be conducted during scheduled low-activity periods with at least 2 weeks' advance notice to all departments.

title: Nursing Shift Handover Protocol (SBAR)
content: Nursing shift handover must be conducted in person at the bedside for every patient using the SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) framework. Handover must begin no later than 15 minutes before shift end; incoming nurses must arrive on time to receive handover before outgoing nurses leave. The SBAR report for each patient must include: current vital signs, active problems and diagnoses, outstanding orders and pending results, medications administered during the shift including time of last PRN dose, IV access status and infusion rates, any deterioration events or escalations during the shift, and the care plan for the next 8 hours. Handover must be documented in the HIS Nursing Notes module within 30 minutes of shift commencement by the incoming nurse. Patients must be introduced to the incoming nurse during bedside handover; family members present may briefly observe unless the patient objects. All outstanding critical tasks must be personally handed over verbally — do not leave critical actions documented only in HIS without a verbal alert.

title: Medication Administration Safety Standards
content: Medication administration must follow the 10 Rights: Right Patient, Right Drug, Right Dose, Right Route, Right Time, Right Documentation, Right Reason, Right Response, Right Expiry, Right Form. Patient identity must be verified using two identifiers (MRN wristband and patient-stated name) before every medication administration; verbal verification alone is insufficient. High-alert medications (insulin, anticoagulants, concentrated electrolytes, chemotherapy agents, opioids) require independent double-check by a second registered nurse before administration; both nurses must sign the Medication Administration Record (MAR). Medications must be administered within 30 minutes before or after the scheduled time; deviations must be documented with reason. Any medication error or near-miss must be reported in the HIS Quality Module within 1 hour of discovery, regardless of whether patient harm occurred. Nurses must NOT administer medications from unlabeled syringes or containers; prepared but unlabeled medications must be discarded.

title: Patient Fall Prevention and Post-Fall Assessment
content: All inpatients must be assessed for fall risk within 4 hours of admission using the Morse Fall Scale (MFS) in the HIS Nursing Module; patients scoring ≥45 are High Risk and require immediate preventive interventions. High-risk patients must have a yellow FALL RISK wristband applied, bed alarms activated, call bell within reach, and a bed in the lowest position. Non-slip footwear, adequate lighting, and clear pathways must be maintained at all times; high-risk patients should not be left in the bathroom or shower without supervision. Fall prevention education must be provided to the patient and family within 24 hours of high-risk identification and documented in HIS. If a patient falls, do not move the patient; call for immediate nursing assistance and notify the physician within 10 minutes. A post-fall assessment must be completed within 30 minutes covering injury assessment, vital signs, neurological status, and circumstances of the fall. The fall must be reported in the HIS Quality Module within 1 hour as an incident; the quality team will review contributing factors and update fall risk protocols quarterly based on incident trends.

title: Procurement Request and Purchase Order Procedure
content: All procurement requests must be submitted through the HIS Supply Chain Module by the requesting department head; verbal or informal procurement requests are not accepted. The request must include: item description, specifications, quantity, clinical or operational justification, required-by date, and budget code. Requests below $1,000 are approved by the Department Head; $1,000–$5,000 require Supply Chain Manager approval; amounts above $5,000 require Finance Director sign-off and a minimum of three competitive quotations. Emergency procurement (for patient safety-critical items) may be verbally authorized by the Operations Manager and must be formally documented within 4 hours. All approved purchase orders must be issued on hospital letterhead or through the HIS; no verbal orders to vendors are permitted. Goods received must be inspected against the purchase order for quantity, specifications, and expiry dates before acceptance; discrepancies must be notified to the vendor and Supply Chain Manager within 24 hours.

title: Inventory Reorder and Stock Management Policy
content: Each department is responsible for maintaining minimum and maximum stock levels for all consumables and supplies, as defined in the department's Stock Management Plan filed with the Supply Chain team. HIS-generated low-stock alerts trigger automatic reorder notifications to the Supply Chain team when inventory falls below the reorder point (ROP); departments must NOT wait for stock-out before raising a request. The Supply Chain team must process standard reorder requests within 48 hours and communicate expected delivery timelines to the requesting department. All stock movements (receipts, issues, returns, disposals) must be recorded in HIS in real time; manual stock registers are not acceptable except during system downtime. Expired, damaged, or recalled stock must be quarantined immediately, tagged clearly, and reported to the Supply Chain Manager and Quality team for safe disposal within 24 hours. A full physical inventory count must be conducted quarterly; results must be reconciled with HIS within 5 business days and variances above 2% reported to the Finance Controller.

title: Emergency Department Triage Protocol (ESI 5-Level)
content: All patients presenting to the Emergency Department must be triaged by a registered nurse within 3 minutes of arrival using the Emergency Severity Index (ESI) 5-level system. ESI 1 (Immediate): life-threatening conditions requiring resuscitation — patient brought directly to resuscitation bay, physician notified immediately. ESI 2 (Emergent): high-risk situation or severe pain — seen within 10 minutes. ESI 3 (Urgent): two or more resources anticipated — seen within 30 minutes. ESI 4 (Less Urgent): one resource anticipated — seen within 60 minutes. ESI 5 (Non-Urgent): no resources anticipated — seen within 120 minutes. Triage assessment must be documented in the HIS Emergency Module immediately. Pediatric patients, pregnant women, and patients with altered consciousness must be triaged at ESI 2 or higher pending full assessment. Patients who deteriorate while waiting must be re-triaged immediately; nursing staff must reassess all ESI 3–5 patients every 30 minutes. The Charge Nurse must alert the Emergency Physician of ambulance arrivals pre-hospital.

title: Mass Casualty Incident (MCI) Activation and Response Plan
content: A Mass Casualty Incident is declared when the number and/or severity of casualties exceeds the Emergency Department's routine capacity. MCI activation is authorized by the Emergency Department Head, Medical Superintendent, or the most senior physician on duty; activation triggers the hospital-wide MCI Plan. The Medical Director must notify all on-call staff and request cancellation of all elective procedures; available beds must be freed within 30 minutes of activation. The SMART (Simple Triage and Rapid Treatment) triage system is used during MCIs to categorize patients: Immediate (Red), Delayed (Yellow), Minimal (Green), Expectant (Black). Dedicated MCI command posts must be established at the ED entrance and hospital command center; media communication is handled exclusively by the designated Public Relations Officer. Deactivation of the MCI Plan is authorized only by the Medical Superintendent after confirming all casualties have been stabilized or transferred. A post-event debrief and documentation review must occur within 48 hours of MCI deactivation.
